## 2.4.1.1. Culture:

- >A critical element of achieving Beyond Zero is having a good health and safety culuure. A workplace culture can be characterized as being 'the way we do things round here'. It is macdleup attitudes, behaviors, levels of competence and the way we behave.
- A good health and safety culture will existwherehealth and safety awareness and controls are integrated into day-to-day organizational management practices, such as having positive attitudes, positive beliefs and positive behavior with regards to health and safety.
- Creating a good health and safety culture requires a common vision and effort from everyone. Research has demonstrated that the management philosophy of an organization is the most importantfactor determiningitshealth and safetyperformance.

Ref: EGY/PRJCTS/HSE/REQs

## 2.4. Zero Harm

- Zero Harm is the philosophy which shall be used on all construction sites to keep people, the environment and assetssafe.That means noindividual or other assetisinjured,harmed or otherwise and not allowing unsafe practices, behaviors, or conditions to exist. It's about creating a culture of
- The journey towards zeroincidents and injuriesfostered by a culture of caringwhere themindset of safeworking is ingrained shall become a'way of life'for staff.Beyond Zerois the means to reach this objective and is fundamental to employees and stakeholders and to EMAAR Misr business in thc long tcrm.
- The Zero Harm approach can be summarized by:
- Overall leadership and communication in a clear and consistent manner,
- Direct hands-on guidance and leadership,
- Sharing and endorsement of best practice,
- Ongoing support to all our staff as required,
- ?Proinotion of the benefits and positive aspects of a good health and safety culture,
- Reinforcement of the importance of engagement with clients, partners and suppliers,
- Support to the concept of safety in design as a key contributor to construction safety
- Supporting Zero Harm are 5 key health and safety principles:
- All accidents are preventable
- ·Health and safety is led from the top, down
- cEveryone is responsible for health and safety
- ·Positive behaviors to be reinforced with negative behaviors challenged
- ·Everyone has the right to stop work or to stop others from working if it is unsafe, without fear of any action taken against thatperson
